root_causes.condition: The Chaos Mesh schedule repeatedly spawned NetworkChaos experiments that partitioned the checkout pod from both Kafka pods.
root_causes.name: otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition

diagnosis.summary: The Chaos Mesh Schedule launched a new checkout-to-Kafka network-partition experiment every minute. Each experiment disrupted checkout's Kafka orders producer, causing Kafka write failures and an open circuit breaker; checkout requests then timed out at frontend-proxy as 504s, producing the elevated error-rate and latency alerts.

agent_messages: I’m using Wayfinder because you explicitly requested it; I’ll keep its state mapping lightweight while performing a read-only forensic investigation of the recorded snapshot.

The routing contract confirms this is a read-only diagnosis, so I will not create Wayfinder state or modify the snapshot. I’m now enumerating the recorded Kubernetes evidence and tracing causes upstream from unhealthy workloads.

The decisive evidence is a Chaos Mesh schedule that continuously creates NetworkChaos runs against checkout and both Kafka pods. Those runs match the checkout Kafka failures and the frontend-proxy 504/latency alert; the pod health and control-plane alerts are downstream or unrelated signals.

Diagnosis completed and saved to [diagnosis.json](/var/folders/qt/4kz3_8fn6hx612tyl9tj4dbm0000gn/T/.itbench-wayfinder-v1-runs-76df38a82288/s80-c-r1/workspace/diagnosis.json).

It identifies the single upstream cause: the Chaos Mesh `Schedule` repeatedly partitioning checkout from Kafka. JSON schema validation passed.
